### 1 of 1. 2 unused imports in the widget files can be removed

### What was found
Two lines that bring in code from another file never use it. One is at src/widgets/render.ts line 2 and one is at src/widgets/format.ts line 3. Both lines are in the parts of the files that this pull request changed.

### Why it matters
Code that is brought in but never used makes a file harder to read and suggests a connection that does not exist. The housekeeping base rules, in their Code section, say to remove imports, variables and modules that nothing uses.

### What happens if you accept
The two unused lines are deleted. That change goes into one commit, which is pushed to the existing pull request branch, feature/widget-colors. These issues were found by reading the files, so no test will be rerun.

Pick one:
1. [ ] Fix - Make one commit for this class and push it to the existing PR branch. [recommended]
2. [ ] Ignore - leave them as they are

gauntlet: gate=housekeeping/card recommended=1

### 1 of 1. Two unused imports in the widget files are not needed

### What was found
`src/widgets/render.ts:2` and `src/widgets/format.ts:3` each import a name that the file never uses. Both lines are within the PR’s changed line ranges.

### Why it matters
The housekeeping base rules, **Code**, require removing unused imports, unused variables and modules with no caller. Neither import is used, so removing them follows the rule directly. No repository rule overrides this check.

### What happens if you accept
Remove the two import lines, make one commit for this class, and push it to the existing draft PR’s branch. Verification will check that the imports are gone; no command that repeats a failing action is attached to this read-only check.

Pick one:
1. [ ] Fix — Make one commit for this class and push it to the existing PR branch. [recommended]
2. [ ] Ignore — Leave them as they are.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Nothing regressed: After keeps every fact Before kept, and it additionally satisfies card-prose, which Before failed because its title was the bare check id ("Card 1 of 1: code-unused") and it used labeled fields (Rule, Findings, Verification, Delivery) instead of the three plain-prose sections. After's title carries count, noun, place and predicate, the Fix row now states the one-commit-to-existing-PR-branch promise directly rather than leaving it to a separate Delivery line, the checkboxes are empty with the recommendation carried only by the [recommended] label, and no Ticket pick appears on this PR card. One small tightening to consider: the Fix row and Ignore row use different capitalization styles ("Make one commit..." vs "leave them as they are"); align them, and keep the explicit branch name in the "What happens if you accept" section as you have, since that is what anchors same-pr-commit when the delivery is commit-push rather than a per-class PR.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Nothing moved from holds to fails; After keeps every fact Before kept and additionally satisfies same-pr-commit and card-prose, which Before failed because its Fix row only said "Remove both imports" with delivery buried in a separate line that never named the existing PR branch or a single commit, and its title ("Card 1 — Unused imports") lacked a count/place/predicate and the three prose sections. After's Fix row ("Make one commit for this class and push it to the existing PR branch"), the empty `[ ]` boxes with a `[recommended]` label on exactly one pick, and the titled sections deliver the Change cleanly. One wording nit that does not move a fact: "no command that repeats a failing action is attached" is an awkward gloss on "regression command"; plainer would be "this is a read-only check, so no test command is run afterward" — that keeps the everyday-prose requirement without inventing a definition the reader has to decode.
